01 / Scope

One closed local experiment joining granularity, collapse and the carrier, with its gravitational and curvature comparisons

Question. Do the actual outputs of G1, C1, GA1 and FC1 work together on D2's internal spin geometry, including records, exchange and gravity (§9)? The keys G1, C1, GA1, FC1, D2, D3, D4 and D5 are the citation keys of the source table in §9.

Proposed result. Under the registered premises, granularity, collapse, geometric actions and the carrier operate consistently on the internal spin geometry (Verdict). In one closed local experiment a prepared internal spin wave exchanges torque with its source apparatus, selects a complete record, becomes an admitted spatial carrier, exerts the derived overlap force and is captured. Each supported outcome conserves the complete local energy, momentum, angular momentum and admitted action, eventwise:

SC32
\[H_{\rm loc}^{\rm final}=H_{\rm loc}^{\rm initial},\qquad P_E+P_R=0,\qquad\mathbf{L}_E+\mathbf{S}_R=0,\qquad Q_R=Q=s_*.\]

The same complete energy supplies D4's gravitational response (SC37, SC55–SC56), and the derived spatial connection gives a definite curvature-dependent spin comparison (SC48–SC49).

1.2 Common obligations that do not apply

Each item below is a frequently requested check that none of this document's claims or adopted premises entails. The reason is quoted from the document. Nothing here waives a requirement of a claim the document makes.

  • Assigning every species, deriving exchange statistics, or executing a decay theory. “The result concerns the existing massive spin doublet and this interaction; it does not assign every species, derive exchange statistics or execute a decay theory” (§10); “no decay transition, product or rate is added by this integration” (§20).
  • Independent experimental confirmation of the calibration and of the physical choices. “Empirical calibration s* = ℏ is retained, as are the physical choices of sector, couplings and conditional uniform apparatus-phase preparation. Their independent experimental confirmation is not claimed” (§10). The checks of §19 verify the stated construction.
  • Uniqueness of the completions. The claim is sufficiency: “These are sufficient compatible completions” (§10); SC-COV is “A selected curved-wave completion” (§10).
  • A new flight integration. “Since the spatial Hamiltonian is identity on spin, the integrated solution is exactly” SC29; “No new flight integration or fitted impulse is needed” (§15).
  • General exterior packet trajectories. “General exterior packet trajectories are not substituted for that solved limit” (§10); “The completed local interaction below uses the exact constant-coefficient limit” (§16).
  • Translation balance of a general extended exterior system. “Local translation balance is claimed for the selected laboratory Hamiltonian; a general extended exterior system would include its source/support exchanges and the appropriate symmetry charges” (§10). The stationary support's exchange of gravitational momentum belongs to that external account (§16).
  • A general moving-boost transport law. “A general moving-boost transport law is not inferred from a scalar clock factor” (§11, row T1).
  • Dissipation of a higher-mode input into the ground sector. “The least-energy bound and gap are mathematical results; they do not themselves dissipate a higher-mode input into the ground sector. The present experiment starts in the already-declared prepared sector” (§11).
  • A minimum length or a universal duration. “No minimum length or universal duration follows from SC10 alone” (§13). The event time follows from the overlap rate and the action threshold, SC24.
  • Preservation of orientation area by the collapse selection. Its fixed-axis reduced orientation map has zero \(\mathsf G\) pullback; it “preserves admission and the complete charges with the apparatus; it need not preserve orientation area” (§13).
  • FC1's common-polarization capture chart under position-dependent transport. Such transport across an extended packet “need not preserve FC1's common-polarization capture chart; the solved laboratory uses the common frame and the exterior comparison has the separately specified domain” (§17).
  • An identification of the different curvatures. \({\rm Ric}(h)=C\) “is calculated for this metric; it does not identify the spatial curvature two-form, clock Hessian, unit internal-sphere curvature RK=6 or coefficient action curvature with each other” (§17).
  • Feeding the state-volume metric back into the internal wave. \(\gamma=\chi^4h\) “is not fed back into the fixed round K wave equation” (§17).
  • Identifying the static and free-fall slicings throughout an extended experiment. “agreement at that origin does not identify the two slicings throughout an arbitrary extended radial experiment” (§10).
  • A strict signal-front theorem, or a Born rule for the capture. The embedded FC1 input states: “The group velocity and computed finite registration time are not a strict signal-front theorem”, and “The single phase-anchored capture channel is an explicitly adopted complete event, not a Born rule inferred from overlap” (§19, embedded FC1 input).
  • A second spin measurement at the receiver. “The receiver's arrival label does not erase the stored spin or substitute for a second spin measurement” (§18).
  • An extra dwell interval or a second trigger. The intermediate C1-only values “factor the one event algebraically; they are not an extra dwell interval or a second trigger” (§15).
  • A mechanical transport protocol for the comparison loop. The exterior connection loop “is a spatial comparison of frames, not an extra material journey added to the interaction ledger” (§10); the geometry script states that the finite comparison “is not a mechanical transport protocol” (§19).

02 / Method

One finite route: one geometry, one Hamiltonian, one joint event and one reused flight, then the same account on two clocks and along two paths

2.1 The calculation route

The calculation is finite. It fixes one internal geometry and one autonomous local Hamiltonian, solves the motion before the event exactly, applies one joint event at the action threshold, reuses one verified flight through an exact identity, and closes the ledger at capture. It then reads the same complete account on the reference clock of a held location and compares spin frames along two paths of the supplied exterior. The equations carry each part; the table names them.

2.2 Thought experiments

The first experiment is the document's own solved experiment. The others are the document's further experiments and checks. Each states its participants, operations, observer, clock, ruler and reference, the quantity calculated with its equations, and the obligation it fulfils.

GCS-X01 · The integrated experiment (§18, built in §14–§15)

Participants and initial dataSource body at \(x_E=-30\): bare energy 1000; bound packet \(\zeta_E(0)=(\sqrt3/2,1/2)^T\) with \(Q=s_*\); full top with \(R=1\), \(\mathbf n=\mathbf e_3\), \(\mathbf L_E=-\mathbf S_E\), \(\mathcal J=5\); buffer \(B_E=10\) with \(M_b=1\), \(\nu=0.7\); ready record \(E_{r,E}=0.025\); coupling \(\varepsilon_E=0.45\), so \(\Gamma=0.1\) and \(\bar\omega=0.55\). Receiver at \(x_R=0\): bare energy 1000, empty bound slot, buffer 10, ready-record energy 0.2. Channel: \(L_c=160\), \(n=-80,\dots,80\), \(k_0=1\), \(\sigma_k=0.15\), \(a_w=4\), \(\varepsilon_R=0.1\); empty carrier, \(b=0\).
Operations and allowed exchangesContinuous torque between the bound spin and the top through \(-\Gamma\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf S_E\) SC12. At the action threshold, one source event on one slice: selection by the buffer phase, recoil of the top, the written record, the buffer reset and the emission of the selected coefficient into the aperture SC25–SC28. Flight under the overlap force, exchanging momentum between carrier and receiver SC18–SC19. Capture by the receiver's complete root SC30–SC31. No external switching; all centre motion collinear with \(\mathbf d\).
Observer, clock, ruler and referenceThe laboratory's local time \(\tau\) on the common slice; each body's proper clock \(\mathcal R_j/H_j\) after recoil; the channel coordinate \(x\) along \(\mathbf d\). Units \(E_0=s_*\omega_0\), \(p_0=s_*\omega_0/c\), \(\ell_0=c/\omega_0\), \(\tau_0=1/\omega_0\).
Quantity and equations\(\tau_E\) and \(p_\pm\) SC24; \(\zeta_\sigma\), \(\mathbf S_\sigma\), \(\mathbf L_E^+\) SC25, SC52; \(H_E^+,\mathcal R_E^+,B_E^+,P_E^+\) SC53; the flight of 41.90159120135437 local time units SC29; \(H_R^+,\mathcal R_R^+,B_R^+\) SC54; \(\zeta_R^+\) SC31; the ledger and SC32.
ObligationsGCS-O05–GCS-O14.

A faithful explanatory version. Two bodies sit 30 length units apart on one line. The first holds one spinning packet, a free top, a spring and a three-position switch; the second holds an empty slot, a spring and an arrival switch. The packet and the top twist each other, and their total twist stays zero. A running total of the packet's overlap with the top grows at a steady rate; when it reaches one unit of action, at once, the packet takes one of the two directions along the top's axis, the top takes the opposite twist, the first switch records the sign, and the packet leaves as a wave along the line, while the spring's energy is reset so that every energy is counted. The wave pushes on the second body through their overlap and is caught whole by its slot, whose switch records the arrival and which keeps the packet's spin. For these prepared spin data, which direction is taken depends on where the first spring was in its cycle at that moment. The participants, the operations and the clocks are those of the table above.

It checks the composition of GCS-X01's one event; it is not an extra dwell interval or a second trigger.

03 / Premises

Thirty-four material inputs, each with its status and its appendix

The register lists the material inputs the calculation actually uses. Definitions fix symbols and the local model (GCS-P31). D2's retained premises are imported as the inputs they are in D2 (GCS-P01–P09). Imported results were derived in their sources under the premises named there (GCS-P10, P11, P20–P22, P25–P27). Selected completions were adopted in their sources and are imported with that status (GCS-P11's C-LIFT and C-DOMAIN, GCS-P13–P19, P23). Three new compatible completions are stated by this document; they are sufficient, not unique, and SC-COV is one selected completion (GCS-P28–P30). The calibration is an empirical anchor (GCS-P12). The flight is a reported numerical result, inherited and independently checked here (GCS-P24). Preparations fix the data of the solved experiment and of the comparisons (GCS-P32–P34). Necessary and sufficient conditions are kept apart: readiness requires SC28 for every supported outcome together with C1's positive intermediate-buffer domain (GCS-A28), while the three completions are sufficient for the construction.

One appendix for each premise

Each appendix states its premise, upstream inputs, foundation or derivation, domain and status, and links back to the premise and the obligations that use it. An adopted input (a definition, an imported result, a selected completion, a calibration, a preparation) is identified as an input, and the checks and consequences this document calculates for it are shown. Where the document derives a consequence, its own equations are transcribed with the intermediate steps. Key equations stay visible; longer material is in the expandable blocks.

GCS-A01 · Physical rotations act on the internal coefficients (for GCS-P01, the document's M1)

Premise GCS-P01 · retained root physical premise of D2, imported · used for GCS-O05, GCS-O10, GCS-O19, GCS-O20, GCS-O21

SC08
\[g(\mathbf{a},\theta)=e^{-i\theta\mathbf{a}\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}/2},\qquad T_g\Phi_\zeta=\Phi_{g\zeta},\qquad b_n\mapsto gb_n.\]

Statement. The left lift of an actual spatial rotation acts on every internal coefficient: \(T_g\Phi_\zeta=\Phi_{g\zeta}\) on a bound slot and \(b_n\mapsto gb_n\) on the carrier. “The carrier and bound slots transform with the same physical rotation lift” (§12). The identification is an input: “The identification with actual spatial rotations remains” (§11, row M1).

Provenance, and the consequences this document calculates

Provenance. D2's premise M1, “Physical rotations act through the left lift”, with its foundation in D2's “Appendix M1 — Physical rotation identification” and “The half-angle is calculated”.

Consequences calculated here. Composition is ordinary \(SU(2)\) multiplication, and the spin charges are functions of the coefficients:

§12
\[g(2\pi)=-1,\qquad g(4\pi)=1,\qquad \mathbf S=\tfrac12\zeta^\dagger\boldsymbol\sigma\zeta,\qquad \mathbf S_c=\tfrac12\sum_nb_n^\dagger\boldsymbol\sigma b_n.\]

For common polarization \(b_n=\beta_nu\) the spin magnitude is \(Q/2\); the representation Casimir \(3Q^2/4\) is a different quantity from the squared vector charge \(Q^2/4\). Rotating one of two coherent positive-axis paths by \(\theta\) (GCS-X03) gives the calibrated constructive-port fraction

§12
\[\frac{|1+e^{-i\theta/2}|^2}{4}=\frac{1+\cos(\theta/2)}{2}=\cos^2\frac\theta4,\]

which vanishes at \(2\pi\) and returns at \(4\pi\). D2's doublet action, composition and half-angle follow from M1 and the constructed modes (§11).

Checks made in this document. One simultaneous rotation of apparatus, channel, coefficients, recoil and capture (GCS-X06) leaves every covariance error below \(2.8\times10^{-14}\) (§19 results). Under a passive component change \(\tilde b=S(x)b\), \(\tilde A=SAS^{-1}-(dS)S^{-1}\), and curvature changes tensorially (§17).

Domain and status. A retained root physical premise of D2, imported as an input; it acts on every bound and spatial coefficient slot.

The derivation of the coupling, as this document makes it

Derivation. With SC06 and the Haar identities \(\langle m_i\rangle=0\), \(\langle m_im_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}/3\):

SC07
\[\int_Kw_{\mathbf n}e_\zeta\,d\mu=\omega_0\int_K(1+\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf m)\Big(Q+\frac23\,\mathbf m\cdot\mathbf S\Big)d\mu=\omega_0\Big(Q+\frac23\,n_iS_j\langle m_im_j\rangle\Big)=\omega_0\Big(Q+\frac29\,\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf S\Big),\]

so \(H_{{\rm int},E}=-\varepsilon_E\omega_0Q_E-\Gamma\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf S_E\) with \(\Gamma=2\varepsilon_E\omega_0/9\). In coefficient form the energy-form matrix is \(\omega_0[1+\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma/9]\). The amplitude pairing \(\int_Kw_{\mathbf n}\rho_\zeta\,d\mu=Q+\frac23\,\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf S\) “would have 1/3 in that position”; “replacing one by the other would change the physical torque coefficient” (§12).

The connection and curvature, derived step by step from the coframe

Torsion-free and metric compatible. With \(e^1=dr/f\), \(e^2=r\,d\theta\), \(e^3=r\sin\theta\,d\phi\) and \(f=f(r)\),

SC43
\[de^1=0,\qquad de^2=dr\wedge d\theta,\qquad de^3=\sin\theta\,dr\wedge d\phi+r\cos\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi.\]

With SC43 and \(\omega^a{}_b=-\omega^b{}_a\) (metric compatibility in the orthonormal coframe), the connection terms are

SC43
\[\begin{aligned} \omega^1{}_2\wedge e^2+\omega^1{}_3\wedge e^3&=-fr\,d\theta\wedge d\theta-fr\sin^2\theta\,d\phi\wedge d\phi=0=-de^1,\\ \omega^2{}_1\wedge e^1+\omega^2{}_3\wedge e^3&=d\theta\wedge dr-r\sin\theta\cos\theta\,d\phi\wedge d\phi=-de^2,\\ \omega^3{}_1\wedge e^1+\omega^3{}_2\wedge e^2&=\sin\theta\,d\phi\wedge dr+r\cos\theta\,d\phi\wedge d\theta=-de^3, \end{aligned}\]

so \(de^a+\omega^a{}_b\wedge e^b=0\) for \(a=1,2,3\).

Curvature. The rotation vector of SC44 has components \(\omega^1=\omega^3{}_2=\cos\theta\,d\phi\), \(\omega^2=\omega^1{}_3=-f\sin\theta\,d\phi\), \(\omega^3=\omega^2{}_1=f\,d\theta\). With \(\mathcal F^a=d\omega^a+\omega^{a+1}\wedge\omega^{a+2}\) (indices cyclic, as in the geometry script) and \(f'=df/dr=L_g/(2r^2f)\), \(1-f^2=L_g/r\):

SC45
\[\begin{aligned} \mathcal F^1&=-\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi+f^2\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi=-\frac{L_g}{r}\sin\theta\,d\theta\wedge d\phi=-\frac{L_g}{r^3}\,e^2\wedge e^3,\\ \mathcal F^2&=-f'\sin\theta\,dr\wedge d\phi=\frac{L_g}{2r^3}\,e^3\wedge e^1,\qquad \mathcal F^3=f'\,dr\wedge d\theta=\frac{L_g}{2r^3}\,e^1\wedge e^2. \end{aligned}\]

These are SC45; the sectional curvatures and the commutator follow as SC46, with \(R_h=2(K_{12}+K_{13}+K_{23})=0\). “The vanishing scalar Rh does not remove these curvature components” (§17). Along a general path, transport is \(U_\gamma=\mathcal P\exp(-\int A)\) (§17).

Provenance. D2's premise T1, with D2's “Appendix T1 — Explicit exterior comparison frame” and “One consistent set of clocks, rulers and spin comparisons”; the exterior is D4's (GCS-A25).

Checks made in this document. The exact checks “levi_civita_structure”, “rotation_curvature_two_forms”, “sectional_ricci_curvature” and “spin_lift_curvature_sign” pass (§19); the last confirms that \(A=-\frac i2\boldsymbol\omega\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma\) gives the stated plus-cross-product curvature.

\[i\frac{db}{d\tau}=[\mathsf{D}-\varepsilon_R\mathcal{E}(X_R)]b,\qquad \frac{dX_R}{d\tau}=\frac{c^2P_R}{H_R},\qquad F_R=\frac{dP_R}{d\tau}=\varepsilon_Rb^\dagger\mathcal{E}'(X_R)b.\]
SC19
\[\frac{dP_c}{d\tau}=-F_R,\qquad \frac{d}{d\tau}(H_R+E_c+U_R)=0,\qquad \frac{d\mathbf{S}_c}{d\tau}=0.\]

Statement. FC1's positive spatial energy matrix, with the periodized Gaussian of FC22–23 and the normalized measure \(dx/L_c\). “Its numerator contains temporal, spatial-gradient and internal-gradient energy. The bound 0≤ℰ≤D yields positive interacting carrier energy for 0<εR<1”; “Translation covariance ℰ′=−i[K,ℰ] proves the first identity; Hermitian spatial dynamics and the body work term prove the second. The third follows because the spatial matrix is identity on spin” (§14).

The three proofs, written out from SC16–SC18

Write \(K={\rm diag}(k_n)\) and \(M=\mathsf D-\varepsilon_R\mathcal E(X_R)\), each acting as the identity on the internal doublet, so that \(i\,db/d\tau=Mb\), \(E_c+U_R=b^\dagger Mb\) and \(P_c=b^\dagger Kb\).

SC19
\[\begin{aligned} \mathcal E'_{mn}&=i(k_n-k_m)\,\mathcal E_{mn}=-i[K,\mathcal E]_{mn},\\ \frac{dP_c}{d\tau}&=i\,b^\dagger[M,K]\,b=-i\varepsilon_R\,b^\dagger[\mathcal E,K]\,b=-\varepsilon_R\,b^\dagger\mathcal E'b=-F_R,\\ \frac{d}{d\tau}\big(E_c+U_R\big)&=b^\dagger\frac{\partial M}{\partial X_R}b\,\frac{dX_R}{d\tau}=-F_R\frac{dX_R}{d\tau},\qquad \frac{dH_R}{d\tau}=\frac{c^2P_R}{H_R}\frac{dP_R}{d\tau}=F_R\frac{dX_R}{d\tau},\\ \frac{d\mathbf S_c}{d\tau}&=\frac i2\,b^\dagger\big[M,1\otimes\boldsymbol\sigma\big]\,b=0. \end{aligned}\]

The second line uses \([\mathsf D,K]=0\); the third adds to zero, which is the energy identity; the fourth holds because \(M\) is the identity on spin. Positivity: for \(0\lt\varepsilon_R\lt1\) and \(0\le\mathcal E\le\mathsf D\), \(b^\dagger[\mathsf D-\varepsilon_R\mathcal E]b\ge(1-\varepsilon_R)\,b^\dagger\mathsf Db\gt0\) for \(b\ne0\).

GCS-A29 · SC-LAB: the constant-clock laboratory and its common slice (for GCS-P29)

Premise GCS-P29 · new compatible completion with a laboratory boundary condition, stated by this document · used for GCS-O15, GCS-O22

SC35
\[\tau=f_0t,\qquad H_{\rm ref}=f_0H_{\rm loc},\qquad W_{\rm ref}=f_0W_{\rm loc},\qquad F_{{\rm interaction,ref}}=f_0F_{{\rm interaction,loc}}.\]
SC36
\[\int W_{\rm ref}\,dt=\int W_{\rm loc}\,d\tau,\qquad \Delta H_{\rm ref}=f_0\Delta H_{\rm loc}=0.\]

Statement. “The constant-f₀ local Hamiltonian and common event slice above; all local Hamiltonian terms are multiplied by the same f₀ in the reference account. The source channel is prepared along the known C1 event axis. The passive receiver remains the FC1 receiver” (§10), with “τ = f₀t, matched to the static held clock at the laboratory origin” (§10).

The boundary condition, its consequences and the size of the approximation

Boundary condition. “The constant-coefficient laboratory is the local approximation to that exterior; it is not asserted to be a finite flat region with the exact exterior's varying f and h. Its dimensions and duration are chosen small relative to the background variation scales” (§10).

Consequences. “Thus the same local states, branch support, Q, spin, momentum and oscillator coordinates give the reference account. Every source, receiver, top, buffer, record, carrier and interaction entry receives f₀. Both event histories reach the same s* at reference times divided by f₀” (§16). At \(f_0=4/5\): \(H_{\rm total,ref}=0.8\times2020.775E_0=1616.62E_0\), \(\Delta H_{\rm total,ref}=0\) SC55, and the reference times of the timing table (§18).

Size of the approximation. For a laboratory ball of proper radius \(a\) with \(\kappa_a=\sup|\operatorname{grad}_h\ln f|\) over it, integrating along the ball gives

§18
\[\Big|\ln\frac f{f_0}\Big|\le\kappa_aa\ \Longrightarrow\ \Big|\frac f{f_0}-1\Big|\le e^{\kappa_aa}-1,\qquad |\operatorname{grad}_h\ln f|_*=\frac{81/(1250L_g)}{4/5}=\frac{81}{1000L_g},\]

so the leading value near \(r_*\) is \(81a/(1000L_g)\); normal-coordinate metric corrections begin at curvature times \(a^2\). “These named approximation parameters govern the exterior interpretation, while SC16 and the local ledger are exact within the selected constant-coefficient model” (§18).

Checks made in this document. “moving_phase_and_history_conversion” verifies \(f_0W_{\rm loc}(\tau/f_0)=W_{\rm loc}\tau\) (§19).

Domain and status. A new compatible completion with a laboratory boundary condition, stated by this document, for the constant-coefficient laboratory.

GCS-A30 · SC-COV: the curved-wave completion (for GCS-P30)

Premise GCS-P30 · new compatible completion, one selected completion, stated by this document · used for GCS-O17

SC38
\[\mathcal{I}_{\rm cov}=\frac{I}{2}\int dt\,d\nu_h\left[f^{-1}|\partial_t\psi|^2-fc^2h^{ij}(D_i\psi)^\dagger D_j\psi-f\omega_0^2|\psi|^2\right].\]
SC39
\[f^{-1}\partial_t^2\psi-\frac{c^2}{\sqrt{|h|}}D_i\left(f\sqrt{|h|}h^{ij}D_j\psi\right)+f\omega_0^2\psi=0.\]

Statement. “A selected curved-wave completion uses the supplied f and h and the T1 covariant derivative in the positive quadratic wave action of §16. It includes no extra scalar-curvature potential. Its constant-f, flat-channel limit is the exact laboratory wave” (§10). The setup: \(\psi(x,t)\) is the carrier's internal-ground coefficient field; \(D_i=\partial_i+A_i\); the static held frame \(A_t=0\); a fixed-normalization volume \(d\nu_h=dV_h/V_{\rm norm}\), a units convention absorbed into \(I\) and not differentiated; closed or no-flux self-adjoint boundary conditions (§16).

The variation, the conserved quantities and the exact reduction

Variation. \(A\) is anti-Hermitian, so \(\partial_i(u^\dagger v)=(D_iu)^\dagger v+u^\dagger D_iv\); with \(d\nu_h=\sqrt{|h|}\,d^3x/V_{\rm norm}\) and no boundary flux, integrating by parts in \(t\) and \(x\) gives

SC39
\[\delta\mathcal I_{\rm cov}=I\operatorname{Re}\int dt\,d\nu_h\,\delta\psi^\dagger\Big[-f^{-1}\partial_t^2\psi+\frac{c^2}{\sqrt{|h|}}D_i\big(f\sqrt{|h|}\,h^{ij}D_j\psi\big)-f\omega_0^2\psi\Big],\]

and \(\delta\mathcal I_{\rm cov}=0\) for every \(\delta\psi\) is SC39.

Conserved quantities. Time and common-phase symmetries give SC40:

SC40
\[H_{\rm cov}=\frac{I}{2}\int\left[f^{-1}|\partial_t\psi|^2+fc^2|D\psi|_h^2+f\omega_0^2|\psi|^2\right]d\nu_h,\qquad Q=-I\int f^{-1}\operatorname{Im}(\psi^\dagger\partial_t\psi)\,d\nu_h.\]

“Both are conserved in the static free problem; Hcov is positive for nonzero data. The spatial stiffness is symmetric in the weighted pairing ∫f−1ψ†ψ dνh, with positive quadratic form ∫f(c²|Dψ|²+ω₀²|ψ|²)dνh” (§16).

Exact reduction. For constant \(f=f_0\), flat \(h\) and \(A=0\), SC39 is \(f_0^{-1}\partial_t^2\psi-c^2f_0\nabla^2\psi+f_0\omega_0^2\psi=0\), and \(\tau=f_0t\) gives FC1's free wave; a frozen-coefficient pure mode \(e^{i(k_ix^i-\omega_{\rm ref}t)}\) gives \(f^{-1}\omega_{\rm ref}^2=f(c^2h^{ij}k_ik_j+\omega_0^2)\), which is SC41:

SC41
\[\partial_\tau^2\psi-c^2\nabla^2\psi+\omega_0^2\psi=0,\qquad \omega_{\rm ref}^2=f^2(\omega_0^2+c^2h^{ij}k_ik_j).\]

“In varying geometry this is its leading local eikonal relation; the full equation is SC39” (§16).

Checks made in this document. “constant_lapse_wave_reduction” and “static_covariant_wave_continuity”: “The wave identities include nonconstant lapse and nonzero connection, so they test the actual additional SC-COV terms” (§19).

Domain and status. A new compatible completion stated by this document, one selected completion among others, in the static exterior with the stated boundary conditions.

08 / Summaries

The seven sections above, for three readers

For a child

This page asks whether four pieces of one picture of nature fit together in one small experiment. Picture two stations on a straight track. The first holds a tiny spinning packet, a free spinning top, a spring and a switch. The packet and the top twist each other back and forth, but their total twist never changes. A counter adds up how strongly the packet touches the top. When the counter reaches one full unit, everything changes at once: the packet points one way or the other along the top's axis, depending on where the spring was in its bounce; the switch clicks into the matching place and stays there; the top takes the twist the packet gave up; the spring's bounce is reset so that no energy goes missing; and the packet leaves as a small wave along the track. The wave pushes the second station a little, and the second station catches it whole and keeps its spin. The page adds up every energy, push and twist at every moment, for both choices, and nothing is lost. Then it shows that the same total energy is what gravity pulls on, and that comparing a spin along two different paths near a heavy round body turns it by 9 degrees. The page lists every rule it uses and where each rule comes from, explains each one, links every answer to its rules and to the computer checks that test it, and lists the tests a finished page must pass.

For a physics teacher

The scope is one closed local experiment built on an internal rotation space \(K=SU(2)\): a source body with a bound two-component spin packet of action \(Q=s_*\), a free spherical top, an oscillator buffer and a record with three stable wells; a periodic spatial channel carrying the emitted wave; and a passive receiver. The method follows the exact precession of spin and top (\(\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf S=1/4\)), accumulates the overlap action until it reaches \(s_*\) at \(\tau_E=40/19\), selects the outcome from the buffer's phase with fractions 3/4 and 1/4 given by the channel-volume square law, gives the top the opposite spin change, writes the record, emits the selected coefficient into a normalized aperture and solves the source's one energy root on the same time slice. The verified flight of the force-carrying excitation is reused through an exact identity, because the spatial dynamics does not act on spin, and the receiver captures the packet with its own energy root. The premises are the spin paper's retained inputs, the granularity paper's admission law and calibration \(s_*=\hbar\), the collapse paper's apparatus and event completions, the force-carrying paper's carrier and capture, the gravity paper's clocks and rulers, and three new completions: the joint event, the constant-clock laboratory and a curved-space wave action. The results: energy, momentum, angular momentum and action are conserved in each outcome separately, with residuals near \(10^{-13}\) from the inherited flight and both final buffers positive; on a held clock with \(f_0=4/5\) every term of the energy takes the same factor while the action does not; gravity acts on the complete stored energy, \(\mathbf F=-\mathcal E\operatorname{grad}_hf\); and the derived spin connection of the gravity paper's rulers rotates a compared spin by 9° between two paths. Section 7 lists 22 completion tests, and all pass.

For a theoretical physicist

On \(K=SU(2)\simeq S^3\) with Haar measure and right character \(k=1\), the lowest doublet has \(\omega_0^2=3\Omega^2\); the energy pairing of the overlap fixes \(\Gamma=2\varepsilon_E\omega_0/9\). G1's action-valued tensor \(\mathsf G\) on \(\mathbb{CP}^{D-1}\), with C-LIFT and C-DOMAIN, admits \(Q_E+Q_c+Q_R=N_Qs_*\). One autonomous Hamiltonian \(H_{\rm loc}=H_E+H_R+b^\dagger[\mathsf D-\varepsilon_R\mathcal E(X_R)]b\), \(0\le\mathcal E\le\mathsf D\), governs source, carrier and receiver. C1's history-dependent event (trigger at \(\int W\,d\tau=s_*\), C-PHASE interval selection, C-END exclusivity, C-JUMP recoil \(\mathbf L_E^+=-\mathbf S_\sigma\) and buffer scaling) is composed by SC-JOINT with emission \(b_n^+=\alpha_ne^{-ik_nX_E}\zeta_\sigma\) and the single root \(B_E^+\); because the spatial generator is \(1\) on spin, \(b^{\rm SC1}=e^{i3}\beta^{\rm FC1}\zeta_\sigma/\sqrt Q\) is exact; capture closes the eventwise balance SC32 in each outcome. On D4's static exterior \(f=\sqrt{1-L_g/r}\), \(h=dr^2/f^2+r^2d\Omega^2\): \(H_{\rm ref}=f_0H_{\rm loc}\) with \(\int W_{\rm ref}\,dt=\int W_{\rm loc}\,d\tau\); the held force is \(-\mathcal E\operatorname{grad}_hf\) on the complete energy; SC-COV is a positive quadratic action with \(D=d-\frac i2\boldsymbol\omega\cdot\boldsymbol\sigma\) that reduces exactly to the laboratory wave; the Levi-Civita spin connection has curvature two-forms with sectionals \((-L_g/2r^3,-L_g/2r^3,L_g/r^3)\), \(R_h=0\), and \({\rm Ric}(h)=C=D_iD_jf/f\) in this exterior; two equatorial paths compare by \(U_{\rm rel}=e^{-i\pi\sigma_2/40}\). Status: SC-JOINT, SC-LAB and SC-COV are sufficient compatible completions, not unique ones; the calibration \(s_*=\hbar\) is an anchor; no field equation, quantum postulate or universal particle classification is imported; the verification is by ten exact symbolic checks and numerical residuals of order \(10^{-13}\) and below. Domain: the prepared doublet, the supported outcomes, a constant-\(f_0\) laboratory with named approximation parameters, and the static exterior \(r\gt L_g\).

19 / Decisive verification of the integration

Check the new boundaries and reuse the proven trajectory

The new joint-event calculation verifies both branches: selected action and spin, the C1 factorization, retained source-top energy, actual source buffer, full complex capture phase, realized oscillator states and the final complete ledger. The final energy residual is 9.10 × 10−13E₀ and the final momentum residual is 6.14 × 10−13p₀, inherited from the completed FC1 numerical solve.

A separate standalone matching script uses five complete 161-mode snapshots from that saved flight, with recorded source hashes and numerical provenance. For both spin outcomes, the SC29 transformation preserves its energy and momentum to 1.34 × 10−15, its force to 8.03 × 10−18, and the captured coefficient phase to 3.48 × 10−16 in the chosen units. The full spin/top residual is at most 2.48 × 10−13, consistent with the prior trajectory's action drift. It also checks the aperture's action-form pullback and one nontrivial simultaneous rotation of the apparatus, channel, coefficients, recoil and capture.

The geometry script passes 10 grouped exact symbolic checks: metric compatibility/torsion, Cartan curvature, independent Christoffel/Ricci calculation, clock Hessian and force, spin-lift sign, finite comparison, phase/rate conversion and the curved-wave energy/action continuity identities. The wave identities include nonconstant lapse and nonzero connection, so they test the actual additional SC-COV terms.

The inherited FC1 N=80 to N=96 refinement changes the flight interval by 4.64 × 10−9τ₀. It applies here through the exact matching identity. The new source event and proper-clock/phase calculations are evaluated separately; old source buffers, absolute times and oscillator coordinates were not copied.

The following complete scripts reproduce the new calculations. The joint-event script embeds its FC1 numerical input, and the matching script embeds its five compressed full-band snapshots. They require Python and NumPy; the exact geometry checks require SymPy. The original FC1 document contains its independent full flight solver. No external file lookup is needed for the scripts embedded here.

Both complete event branches and actual apparatus states — verify_joint_chain.py

      "rms_width": 3.9640511224998805,
      "action_fraction_within_12_of_mean": 0.997108305075558,
      "free_energy_mean_x": -0.5189914549787995,
      "free_energy_rms_width": 3.8787614754980817,
      "free_energy_fraction_within_12_of_mean": 0.9973241426102503
    }
  ],
  "initial_mean_free_group_velocity": 0.7011045044168551,
  "packet_invariant_energy_excess_squared": 0.011406405027513333,
  "no_emission_control": {
    "carrier_Q": 0,
    "carrier_P": 0,
    "receiver_force": 0,
    "receiver_exposure": 0,
    "receiver_click": false
  },
  "scope": [
    "All energies include canonical temporal, spatial-gradient and internal-gradient terms.",
    "The finite-band Hamiltonian and event accounting are exact mathematical definitions; the displayed trajectory is numerical.",
    "The single phase-anchored capture channel is an explicitly adopted complete event, not a Born rule inferred from overlap.",
    "Positive-frequency finite-band packets and periodized Gaussian windows have global tails.",
    "The group velocity and computed finite registration time are not a strict signal-front theorem.",
    "The complete body rest energy changes with internal excitation, oscillator and record energy."
  ],
  "initial_free_energy_centroid_velocity": 0.7050989787085947
}
''')
flight = FC["primary"]

Q = 1.0
omega0 = 1.0
Gamma = 0.1
eps_a = 0.45
baromega = 0.55
J = Q / (2 * Gamma)
B_initial = 10.0
record_ready = Gamma * Q / 4
bare = 1000.0
tau_star = 4 / (19 * Gamma)
alpha_star = np.sqrt(3) * Gamma * tau_star

pauli = np.array([
    [[0, 1], [1, 0]],
    [[0, -1j], [1j, 0]],
    [[1, 0], [0, -1]],
], dtype=complex)

def spin(b):
    return np.array([np.vdot(b, s @ b).real / 2 for s in pauli])

def carray(z):
    return [{"real": float(v.real), "imag": float(v.imag)} for v in np.asarray(z)]

nstar = np.array([
    np.sqrt(3) * (1 - np.cos(alpha_star)) / 4,
    np.sin(alpha_star) / 2,
    (3 + np.cos(alpha_star)) / 4,
])
b0 = np.array([np.sqrt(3) / 2, 0.5], complex)
bstar = np.exp(-1j * (baromega + Gamma / 2) * tau_star) * np.array([
    np.sqrt(3) / 2 * np.cos(alpha_star / 2) + 1j * np.sin(alpha_star / 2),
    0.5 * np.cos(alpha_star / 2),
])
S0 = spin(b0)
Sstar = spin(bstar)
Lstar = -Sstar
rotor_energy = Q * Q / (8 * J)
bound_overlap_before = baromega * Q - Gamma * np.dot(nstar, Sstar)
rest_before = bare + B_initial + record_ready + rotor_energy + bound_overlap_before

field_birth = flight["initial"]["Ec"] - flight["initial"]["W"]
field_momentum_birth = flight["initial"]["Pc"]
source_H_after = rest_before - field_birth
source_P_after = -field_momentum_birth
source_rest_after = np.sqrt(source_H_after**2 - source_P_after**2)
source_buffer_after = source_rest_after - bare - rotor_energy
source_kinetic_after = source_H_after - source_rest_after

capture_old = complex(flight["receiver_amplitude_real"], flight["receiver_amplitude_imag"])
capture_factor = np.exp(3j) * capture_old
flight_time = flight["flight_time"]
total_time = tau_star + flight_time
source_flight_proper_time = source_rest_after / source_H_after * flight_time
receiver_flight_proper_time = FC["realized_buffers"]["receiver_flight_proper_time"]

nu = 0.7
M_buffer = 1.0
chi_R_initial = 0.4
chi_R_final = chi_R_initial + nu * (tau_star + receiver_flight_proper_time)
buffer_R = flight["receiver"]["buffer_after_absorption"]
q_R = np.sqrt(2 * buffer_R / (M_buffer * nu**2)) * np.sin(chi_R_final)
p_R = np.sqrt(2 * M_buffer * buffer_R) * np.cos(chi_R_final)

results = {
    "status": "PASS",
    "units": "s*=omega0=c=1",
    "emission_local_time": tau_star,
    "flight_local_duration_reused_from_FC1": flight_time,
    "absorption_local_time": total_time,
    "channel_unit_direction": nstar.tolist(),
    "initial_spin": S0.tolist(),
    "pre_event_spin": Sstar.tolist(),
    "continuous_spin_change": (Sstar - S0).tolist(),
    "pre_event_spinor": carray(bstar),
    "source": {
        "initial_rest_and_total_energy": rest_before,
        "bound_plus_overlap_before": bound_overlap_before,
        "retained_top_energy": rotor_energy,
        "total_energy_after_emission": source_H_after,
        "momentum_after_emission": source_P_after,
        "rest_energy_after_emission": source_rest_after,
        "buffer_after_emission": source_buffer_after,
        "recoil_kinetic_energy": source_kinetic_after,
        "proper_flight_time": source_flight_proper_time,
    },
    "carrier_birth_interacting_energy": field_birth,
    "capture_transport_phase_factor": carray([capture_factor])[0],
    "receiver": {
        **flight["receiver"],
        "proper_flight_time": receiver_flight_proper_time,
        "buffer_phase_at_capture": chi_R_final,
        "buffer_q_after_capture": q_R,
        "buffer_p_after_capture": p_R,
    },
    "branches": {},
}

for sigma, selector_phase in [(1, np.pi), (-1, 7 * np.pi / 4)]:
    projection = (np.eye(2) + sigma * np.tensordot(nstar, pauli, axes=(0, 0))) / 2
    probability = np.vdot(bstar, projection @ bstar).real / Q
    b_selected = projection @ bstar / np.sqrt(probability)
    S_selected = spin(b_selected)
    L_selected = -S_selected
    delta_spin = S_selected - Sstar
    delta_spin_top_energy = -(Lstar / J + Gamma * nstar) @ delta_spin + np.dot(delta_spin, delta_spin) / (2 * J)
    B_intermediate = B_initial + record_ready - delta_spin_top_energy
    bound_intermediate = baromega * Q - Gamma * np.dot(nstar, S_selected)
    R_intermediate = bare + B_intermediate + rotor_energy + bound_intermediate
    captured = capture_factor * b_selected

    chi_source_initial = selector_phase - nu * tau_star
    chi_source_final = selector_phase + nu * source_flight_proper_time
    q_source = np.sqrt(2 * source_buffer_after / (M_buffer * nu**2)) * np.sin(chi_source_final)
    p_source = np.sqrt(2 * M_buffer * source_buffer_after) * np.cos(chi_source_final)
    observed_buffer = p_source**2 / (2 * M_buffer) + M_buffer * nu**2 * q_source**2 / 2
    initial_total = rest_before + flight["receiver"]["H_before_emission"]
    final_total = source_H_after + flight["receiver"]["H_after_absorption"]

    checks = {
        "selected_Q": abs(np.vdot(b_selected, b_selected).real - Q),
        "selected_spin": float(np.linalg.norm(S_selected - sigma * Q * nstar / 2)),
        "C1_intermediate_energy": abs(R_intermediate - rest_before),
        "spin_top_energy_formula": abs(delta_spin_top_energy - Gamma * Q * (0.25 - sigma / 2)),
        "intermediate_buffer_formula": abs(B_intermediate - (B_initial + sigma * Gamma * Q / 2)),
        "emission_buffer_account": abs((source_buffer_after - B_intermediate) - (bound_intermediate - field_birth - source_kinetic_after)),
        "realized_source_buffer": abs(observed_buffer - source_buffer_after),
        "final_total_energy": abs(final_total - initial_total),
        "final_total_momentum": abs(source_P_after + flight["receiver"]["P_after_absorption"]),
        "final_total_spin": float(np.linalg.norm(L_selected + spin(captured))),
        "capture_action": abs(np.vdot(captured, captured).real - Q),
    }
    assert max(checks.values()) < 3e-11, checks
    assert B_intermediate > 0 and source_buffer_after > 0
    assert 0 < probability < 1

    results["branches"][str(sigma)] = {
        "probability": probability,
        "selected_spinor_before_emission": carray(b_selected),
        "captured_receiver_spinor": carray(captured),
        "spin_after_selection": S_selected.tolist(),
        "top_angular_momentum_after_selection": L_selected.tolist(),
        "collapse_spin_change": delta_spin.tolist(),
        "intermediate_spin_top_energy_change": delta_spin_top_energy,
        "intermediate_buffer": B_intermediate,
        "intermediate_bound_plus_overlap_energy": bound_intermediate,
        "emission_buffer_change_from_intermediate": source_buffer_after - B_intermediate,
        "source_buffer_initial_phase_for_this_example": chi_source_initial,
        "source_buffer_phase_at_selection": selector_phase,
        "source_buffer_phase_at_receiver_capture": chi_source_final,
        "source_buffer_q_at_capture": q_source,
        "source_buffer_p_at_capture": p_source,
        "initial_total_energy": initial_total,
        "final_total_energy": final_total,
        "checks": checks,
    }

(ROOT / "spin_chain_results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
print(json.dumps(results, indent=2))

five states of the completed FC1 N=80 trajectory, not a new flight solution.
It was extracted from flight_data.npz at dense-grid indices
0, 75, 150, 225, 300. The final point is immediately before capture.

The geometric factorization proves all-time matching on the finite domain;
these bounded checks verify the actual numeric data, coefficient phase,
isometric embedding, and simultaneous physical-rotation implementation.

L = 160.0
epsilon_R = 0.1
aw = 4.0
sigma_k = 0.15
k0 = 1.0
source_x = -30.0
k = 2 * np.pi * np.arange(-N, N + 1) / L
omega = np.sqrt(1 + k * k)
delta_k = k[None, :] - k[:, None]
Zw = sum(np.exp(-0.5 * (j * L / aw) ** 2) for j in range(-3, 4))
what = np.sqrt(2 * np.pi) * aw / (L * Zw) * np.exp(-0.5 * aw * aw * delta_k**2)
C = (omega[:, None] * omega[None, :] + k[:, None] * k[None, :] + 1) / (2 * np.sqrt(omega[:, None] * omega[None, :]))
Ebase = C * what
alpha = np.exp(-0.25 * ((k - k0) / sigma_k) ** 2)
alpha /= np.linalg.norm(alpha)

sigma = np.array([
    [[0, 1], [1, 0]],
    [[0, -1j], [1j, 0]],
    [[1, 0], [0, -1]],
], dtype=complex)

def energy_matrix(x):
    return Ebase * np.exp(1j * delta_k * x)

def spin(b):
    a = np.atleast_2d(b)
    return np.array([np.einsum("mi,ij,mj->", a.conj(), s, a).real / 2 for s in sigma])

def quantities(b, x):
    a = np.asarray(b)
    if a.ndim == 1:
        a = a[:, None]
    E = energy_matrix(x)
    q = np.einsum("mi,mi->", a.conj(), a).real
    ec = np.einsum("mi,m,mi->", a.conj(), omega, a).real
    pc = np.einsum("mi,m,mi->", a.conj(), k, a).real
    overlap = epsilon_R * np.einsum("mi,mn,ni->", a.conj(), E, a).real
    force = epsilon_R * np.einsum("mi,mn,ni->", a.conj(), 1j * delta_k * E, a).real
    return np.array([q, ec, pc, overlap, force])

def capture(b, x):
    xi = alpha * np.exp(-1j * k * x)
    anchor_vector = np.einsum("m,mi->i", xi.conj(), b)
    anchor_norm = np.linalg.norm(anchor_vector)
    assert anchor_norm > 0.1
    return np.sqrt(Q) * anchor_vector / anchor_norm, anchor_norm

Gamma = 0.1
J = 5.0
tau_star = 4 / (19 * Gamma)
theta_star = np.sqrt(3) * Gamma * tau_star
nstar = np.array([
    np.sqrt(3) * (1 - np.cos(theta_star)) / 4,
    np.sin(theta_star) / 2,
    (3 + np.cos(theta_star)) / 4,
])
bstar = np.exp(-0.6j * tau_star) * np.array([
    np.sqrt(3) / 2 * np.cos(theta_star / 2) + 1j * np.sin(theta_star / 2),
    0.5 * np.cos(theta_star / 2),
])
Sstar = spin(bstar)
Lstar = -Sstar

rows = []
max_matching = {name: 0.0 for name in ["Q", "Ec", "Pc", "W", "force", "spin", "total_angular_momentum", "source_data"]}
capture_errors = {}
selected = {}

for sign in [1, -1]:
    P = (np.eye(2) + sign * np.tensordot(nstar, sigma, axes=(0, 0))) / 2
    p = np.vdot(bstar, P @ bstar).real / Q
    b_selected = P @ bstar / np.sqrt(p)
    selected[sign] = b_selected
    S_selected = spin(b_selected)
    L_selected = -S_selected

    for i, t in enumerate(times):
        b_new = np.exp(3j) * beta_old[i, :, None] * b_selected[None, :] / np.sqrt(Q)
        original = quantities(beta_old[i], positions[i])
        current = quantities(b_new, positions[i])
        residuals = abs(current - original)
        for name, residual in zip(["Q", "Ec", "Pc", "W", "force"], residuals):
            max_matching[name] = max(max_matching[name], float(residual))
        max_matching["source_data"] = max(max_matching["source_data"], float(np.max(abs(original - fc1_quantities[i]))))
        actual_spin = spin(b_new)
        max_matching["spin"] = max(max_matching["spin"], float(np.linalg.norm(actual_spin - S_selected)))

        # Centres and momenta are all on the prepared nstar channel.
        x_E = source_x * nstar
        p_E = -nstar
        x_R = positions[i] * nstar
        p_R = body_momenta[i] * nstar
        orbital = np.cross(x_E, p_E) + np.cross(x_R, p_R)
        # The source's exact later position is also collinear, so this orbital
        # result is independent of the chosen scalar point on its trajectory.
        total_J = L_selected + actual_spin + orbital
        max_matching["total_angular_momentum"] = max(max_matching["total_angular_momentum"], float(np.linalg.norm(total_J)))
        rows.append({
            "branch": sign,
            "flight_time": float(t),
            "Q": float(current[0]),
            "Ec": float(current[1]),
            "Pc": float(current[2]),
            "W": float(current[3]),
            "force": float(current[4]),
            "spin": actual_spin.tolist(),
            "total_angular_momentum_norm": float(np.linalg.norm(total_J)),
        })

    b_final = np.exp(3j) * beta_old[-1, :, None] * b_selected[None, :] / np.sqrt(Q)
    captured, anchor_norm = capture(b_final, positions[-1])
    expected = np.exp(3j) * captured_scalar_old * b_selected / np.sqrt(Q)
    capture_errors[str(sign)] = {
        "phase_anchor_norm": float(anchor_norm),
        "coefficient_error": float(np.linalg.norm(captured - expected)),
        "spin_error": float(np.linalg.norm(spin(captured) - S_selected)),
        "complete_angular_balance": float(np.linalg.norm(L_selected + spin(captured))),
    }

# The fixed spatial aperture is an isometry for arbitrary comparison vectors.
profile = alpha * np.exp(-1j * k * source_x)
v = np.array([0.2 + 0.3j, -0.4 + 0.1j])
w = np.array([-0.1 + 0.6j, 0.5 - 0.2j])
Ev = profile[:, None] * v[None, :]
Ew = profile[:, None] * w[None, :]
isometry = {
    "profile_norm": float(abs(np.vdot(profile, profile) - 1)),
    "v_norm": float(abs(np.vdot(Ev, Ev) - np.vdot(v, v))),
    "w_norm": float(abs(np.vdot(Ew, Ew) - np.vdot(w, w))),
    "coefficient_inner_product": float(abs(np.vdot(Ev, Ew) - np.vdot(v, w))),
    "action_two_form_pullback": float(abs(2 * np.vdot(Ev, Ew).imag - 2 * np.vdot(v, w).imag)),
}

# One nontrivial simultaneous SU(2)/SO(3) change of physical orientation.
axis = np.array([2.0, -1.0, 3.0]); axis /= np.linalg.norm(axis)
angle = 0.73
g = np.cos(angle / 2) * np.eye(2) - 1j * np.sin(angle / 2) * np.tensordot(axis, sigma, axes=(0, 0))
ax = np.array([[0, -axis[2], axis[1]], [axis[2], 0, -axis[0]], [-axis[1], axis[0], 0]])
R = np.eye(3) * np.cos(angle) + (1 - np.cos(angle)) * np.outer(axis, axis) + np.sin(angle) * ax
nrot = R @ nstar
bstar_rot = g @ bstar
Lstar_rot = R @ Lstar
def spatial_rotation(v, angle):
    cross = np.array([[0, -v[2], v[1]], [v[2], 0, -v[0]], [-v[1], v[0], 0]])
    return np.cos(angle) * np.eye(3) + (1 - np.cos(angle)) * np.outer(v, v) + np.sin(angle) * cross

Caxis = np.array([0.5, 0, np.sqrt(3) / 2])
ez = np.array([0.0, 0.0, 1.0])
top_orientation = spatial_rotation(Caxis, -theta_star) @ spatial_rotation(ez, Gamma * tau_star)
top_orientation_rot = R @ top_orientation
covariance = {name: 0.0 for name in ["spin_vector", "analyser_pairing", "channel_axis", "apparatus_axis", "apparatus_energy", "apparatus_recoil", "selection", "emission", "smooth_quantities", "force_vector", "total_angular_momentum", "capture"]}
covariance["spin_vector"] = float(np.linalg.norm(spin(bstar_rot) - R @ Sstar))
covariance["analyser_pairing"] = float(abs(np.dot(nrot, spin(bstar_rot)) - np.dot(nstar, Sstar)))
covariance["channel_axis"] = float(abs(np.linalg.norm(nrot) - 1))
covariance["apparatus_axis"] = float(np.linalg.norm(top_orientation_rot @ ez - nrot))
covariance["apparatus_energy"] = float(abs(np.dot(Lstar_rot, Lstar_rot) / (2 * J) - np.dot(Lstar, Lstar) / (2 * J)))

for sign in [1, -1]:
    P_rot = (np.eye(2) + sign * np.tensordot(nrot, sigma, axes=(0, 0))) / 2
    p_rot = np.vdot(bstar_rot, P_rot @ bstar_rot).real / Q
    selected_rot = P_rot @ bstar_rot / np.sqrt(p_rot)
    expected_selected_rot = g @ selected[sign]
    covariance["selection"] = max(covariance["selection"], float(np.linalg.norm(selected_rot - expected_selected_rot)))
    emitted_rot = profile[:, None] * selected_rot[None, :]
    emitted_expected = (profile[:, None] * selected[sign][None, :]) @ g.T
    covariance["emission"] = max(covariance["emission"], float(np.linalg.norm(emitted_rot - emitted_expected)))

    i = 3
    b_new = np.exp(3j) * beta_old[i, :, None] * selected[sign][None, :]
    b_rot = b_new @ g.T
    q = quantities(b_new, positions[i]); qr = quantities(b_rot, positions[i])
    covariance["smooth_quantities"] = max(covariance["smooth_quantities"], float(np.max(abs(q - qr))))
    covariance["force_vector"] = max(covariance["force_vector"], float(np.linalg.norm(qr[4] * nrot - R @ (q[4] * nstar))))
    L_selected_rot = -spin(selected_rot)
    covariance["apparatus_recoil"] = max(covariance["apparatus_recoil"], float(np.linalg.norm(L_selected_rot - R @ (-spin(selected[sign])))))
    covariance["total_angular_momentum"] = max(covariance["total_angular_momentum"], float(np.linalg.norm(L_selected_rot + spin(b_rot))))

    final_field = np.exp(3j) * beta_old[-1, :, None] * selected[sign][None, :]
    cap, _ = capture(final_field, positions[-1])
    cap_rot, _ = capture(final_field @ g.T, positions[-1])
    covariance["capture"] = max(covariance["capture"], float(np.linalg.norm(cap_rot - g @ cap)))

assert max(max_matching.values()) < 3e-11, max_matching
assert max(isometry.values()) < 3e-14, isometry
assert max(covariance.values()) < 3e-11, covariance
for values in capture_errors.values():
    assert max(values[key] for key in ["coefficient_error", "spin_error", "complete_angular_balance"]) < 3e-12

results = {
    "status": "PASS",
    "numeric_input_provenance": PROVENANCE,
    "reintegrated": False,
    "snapshot_count": len(times),
    "branches": [1, -1],
    "maximum_matching_errors": max_matching,
    "capture_matching": capture_errors,
    "emission_isometry": isometry,
    "simultaneous_rotation": {"axis": axis.tolist(), "angle": angle, "maximum_errors": covariance},
    "snapshots": rows,
    "scope": [
        "The exact factorization theorem preserves all spatial quadratic forms and the receiver trajectory on the declared common-polarization finite-mode domain.",
        "Five embedded full-band FC1 snapshots check the implementation; they are not a new integration or a universal continuum test.",
        "The source top remains in the complete angular-momentum inventory; all centre motion is collinear with the prepared channel.",
        "The isometry and two-form checks use comparison tangent vectors, not separately admitted extra physical packets.",
        "The capture equality retains the full coefficient phase and both selected spin directions.",
    ],
}
(ROOT / "matching_results.json").write_text(json.dumps(results, indent=2))
print(json.dumps({key: results[key] for key in ["status", "snapshot_count", "maximum_matching_errors", "capture_matching", "emission_isometry", "simultaneous_rotation"]}, indent=2))
Metric, curvature, transport and wave checks — verify_gravity_transport.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exact checks for the bounded gravity/transport completion.

Requires SymPy. No trajectory integration or network access.
Each reported check is one mathematical claim; tensor components are grouped.
"""
from pathlib import Path
import json
import sympy as s

r, L, th, ph = s.symbols("r L_g theta phi", positive=True, real=True)
coords = (r, th, ph)
f = s.sqrt(1-L/r)
ii = s.I
zero1 = s.zeros(3, 1)
checks = []


def flat(items):
    for item in items:
        if isinstance(item, s.MatrixBase):
            yield from list(item)
        elif isinstance(item, (list, tuple)):
            yield from flat(item)
        else:
            yield item


def check(name, meaning, *residuals):
    reduced = [s.simplify(s.trigsimp(x)) for x in flat(residuals)]
    passed = all(x == 0 for x in reduced)
    checks.append(dict(name=name, meaning=meaning, passed=passed,
                       residuals=[str(x) for x in reduced if x != 0]))
    print(("PASS" if passed else "FAIL") + " " + name, flush=True)


def d1(a):
    return s.Matrix(3, 3, lambda j, k:
                    s.diff(a[k], coords[j])-s.diff(a[j], coords[k]))


def wedge(a, b):
    return a*b.T-b*a.T


e = [s.Matrix([1/f, 0, 0]), s.Matrix([0, r, 0]),
     s.Matrix([0, 0, r*s.sin(th)])]
W = [[zero1.copy() for _ in range(3)] for _ in range(3)]
W[0][1] = s.Matrix([0, -f, 0])
W[0][2] = s.Matrix([0, 0, -f*s.sin(th)])
W[1][2] = s.Matrix([0, 0, -s.cos(th)])
for a in range(3):
    for b in range(a+1, 3):
        W[b][a] = -W[a][b]

torsion = [d1(e[a])+sum((wedge(W[a][b], e[b]) for b in range(3)),
                       s.zeros(3)) for a in range(3)]
check("levi_civita_structure",
      "The stated connection solves Cartan's torsion-free equations and is antisymmetric.",
      torsion, [W[a][b]+W[b][a] for a in range(3) for b in range(3)])

Om = [[d1(W[a][b])+sum((wedge(W[a][c], W[c][b]) for c in range(3)),
                       s.zeros(3)) for b in range(3)] for a in range(3)]
w = [W[2][1], W[0][2], W[1][0]]
F = [d1(w[a])+wedge(w[(a+1) % 3], w[(a+2) % 3]) for a in range(3)]
F_expected = [-L/r**3*wedge(e[1], e[2]),
              L/(2*r**3)*wedge(e[2], e[0]),
              L/(2*r**3)*wedge(e[0], e[1])]
check("rotation_curvature_two_forms",
      "Direct exterior differentiation gives SC45 and agrees with the lifted spatial curvature.",
      [F[a]-F_expected[a] for a in range(3)],
      [F[0]-Om[2][1], F[1]-Om[0][2], F[2]-Om[1][0]])

h = s.diag(1/f**2, r**2, r**2*s.sin(th)**2)
hinv = h.inv()
Gamma = [[[s.simplify(sum(hinv[a, d] *
             (s.diff(h[d, b], coords[c])+s.diff(h[d, c], coords[b])
              -s.diff(h[b, c], coords[d]))/2 for d in range(3)))
           for c in range(3)] for b in range(3)] for a in range(3)]
Ric = s.Matrix(3, 3, lambda a, b: s.simplify(sum(
    s.diff(Gamma[k][a][b], coords[k])-s.diff(Gamma[k][a][k], coords[b])
    +sum(Gamma[k][k][j]*Gamma[j][a][b]
         -Gamma[k][b][j]*Gamma[j][a][k] for j in range(3))
    for k in range(3))))
frame = s.diag(f, 1/r, 1/(r*s.sin(th)))
Ric_hat = s.simplify(frame*Ric*frame)
C_expected = s.diag(-L/r**3, L/(2*r**3), L/(2*r**3))
check("sectional_ricci_curvature",
      "Independent metric-Christoffel calculation agrees with the sectionals, nonzero Ricci and zero scalar curvature.",
      Om[0][1]+L/(2*r**3)*wedge(e[0], e[1]),
      Om[0][2]+L/(2*r**3)*wedge(e[0], e[2]),
      Om[1][2]-L/r**3*wedge(e[1], e[2]),
      Ric_hat-C_expected, s.trace(Ric_hat))

Hess = s.Matrix(3, 3, lambda a, b:
                s.diff(f, coords[a], coords[b])
                -sum(Gamma[k][a][b]*s.diff(f, coords[k]) for k in range(3)))
C_hat = s.simplify(frame*Hess*frame/f)
rstar = 25*L/9
Cstar = s.diag(-s.Rational(729, 15625)/L**2,
               s.Rational(729, 31250)/L**2,
               s.Rational(729, 31250)/L**2)
check("frequency_hessian",
      "Clock frequency Hessian matches D4's three time-curvature entries and the selected comparison point.",
      C_hat-C_expected, C_hat.subs(r, rstar)-Cstar,
      f*s.diff(f, r)-L/(2*r**2),
      f*s.diff(f*s.diff(f, r), r)+L*f/r**3)

E = s.symbols("rest_energy", positive=True, real=True)
U = E*(f-1)
Fref = -f*s.diff(U, r)
Floc = Fref/f
check("held_force_and_units",
      "Work per proper ruler gives both force conventions, with exact f*=4/5 coefficients.",
      Fref+E*L/(2*r**2), f*Floc-Fref,
      f.subs(r, rstar)-s.Rational(4, 5),
      Fref.subs(r, rstar)+81*E/(1250*L),
      Floc.subs(r, rstar)+81*E/(1000*L))

sigma = [s.Matrix([[0, 1], [1, 0]]),
         s.Matrix([[0, -ii], [ii, 0]]),
         s.Matrix([[1, 0], [0, -1]])]
aa = s.Matrix(s.symbols("a1:4", real=True))
bb = s.Matrix(s.symbols("b1:4", real=True))
pauli = lambda v: sum((v[j]*sigma[j] for j in range(3)), s.zeros(2))
A = -ii*pauli(aa)/2
B = -ii*pauli(bb)/2
check("spin_lift_curvature_sign",
      "The chosen minus-i/2 spin connection gives the stated plus-cross-product curvature.",
      A*B-B*A+ii*pauli(aa.cross(bb))/2)

alpha = s.symbols("alpha", real=True)
u1 = s.cos(s.Rational(4, 5)*alpha/2)*s.eye(2) \
     -ii*s.sin(s.Rational(4, 5)*alpha/2)*sigma[1]
u2 = s.cos(s.Rational(9, 10)*alpha/2)*s.eye(2) \
     -ii*s.sin(s.Rational(9, 10)*alpha/2)*sigma[1]
rel = u1.conjugate().T*u2
rel_expected = s.cos(alpha/20)*s.eye(2)-ii*s.sin(alpha/20)*sigma[1]
v = s.Matrix([s.cos(s.pi/40), s.sin(s.pi/40)])
Sout = s.Matrix([(v.conjugate().T*sig*v)[0]/2 for sig in sigma])
check("finite_path_comparison",
      "The two supported equatorial paths differ by delta=pi/20 and preserve norm and spin length.",
      rel-rel_expected,
      rel_expected.subs(alpha, s.pi/2)*s.Matrix([1, 0])-v,
      (v.conjugate().T*v)[0]-1,
      Sout-s.Matrix([s.sin(s.pi/20)/2, 0, s.cos(s.pi/20)/2]),
      Sout.dot(Sout)-s.Rational(1, 4))

f0, c, om0, amp, inertia = s.symbols("f0 c omega0 amplitude I", positive=True)
k, vx2, gx2, ax2 = s.symbols("k v_squared gradient_squared amplitude_squared", real=True)
omloc = s.sqrt(om0**2+c**2*k**2)
omref = f0*omloc
Q = inertia*omref*amp**2/f0
H = inertia*(omref**2/f0+f0*(c**2*k**2+om0**2))*amp**2/2
Lref_over_f = inertia*(f0**2*vx2/f0-f0*c**2*gx2-f0*om0**2*ax2)/(2*f0)
Llocal = inertia*(vx2-c**2*gx2-om0**2*ax2)/2
check("constant_lapse_wave_reduction",
      "SC-COV becomes FC1's local action and its pure-mode energy satisfies the D2 inertial relation.",
      Lref_over_f-Llocal, H-Q*omref,
      H**2-f0**2*((Q*om0)**2+c**2*(Q*k)**2))

M, buffer, qb, p, nu, tau, wl = s.symbols(
    "bare_energy buffer Qbound p nu tau Wlocal", positive=True)
rest = M+buffer+om0*qb
Hlocal = s.sqrt(rest**2+c**2*p**2)
Href = f0*Hlocal
check("moving_phase_and_history_conversion",
      "The canonical moving-body derivatives give the redshifted proper phase and invariant event action.",
      s.diff(Href, qb)-f0*om0*rest/Hlocal,
      nu*s.diff(Href, buffer)-f0*nu*rest/Hlocal,
      f0*wl*(tau/f0)-wl*tau)

# A genuinely variable-lapse and nonzero-connection specialization of SC-COV.
# Four real fields represent two complex amplitudes. J is multiplication by i.
x, t = s.symbols("x t", real=True)
fx = s.Function("f")(x)
wx = s.Function("a")(x)
q = s.Matrix([s.Function(n)(x, t) for n in ("u1", "u2", "v1", "v2")])
J = s.BlockMatrix([[s.zeros(2), -s.eye(2)], [s.eye(2), s.zeros(2)]]).as_explicit()
G2 = s.Matrix([[0, -wx/2], [wx/2, 0]])
Ax = s.diag(G2, G2)
Dxq = q.diff(x)+Ax*q
qt = q.diff(t)
qtt = fx*c**2*((fx*Dxq).diff(x)+Ax*(fx*Dxq))-fx**2*om0**2*q
energy = inertia*(qt.dot(qt)/fx+fx*c**2*Dxq.dot(Dxq)+fx*om0**2*q.dot(q))/2
energy_flux = -inertia*fx*c**2*qt.dot(Dxq)
action_density = inertia*(q.T*J*qt)[0]/fx
action_flux = -inertia*fx*c**2*(q.T*J*Dxq)[0]
on_shell = {q[j].diff(t, 2): qtt[j] for j in range(4)}
energy_res = (s.diff(energy, t)+s.diff(energy_flux, x)).subs(on_shell)
action_res = (s.diff(action_density, t)+s.diff(action_flux, x)).subs(on_shell)
check("static_covariant_wave_continuity",
      "A nontrivial variable-lapse, nonzero spin-connection specialization has exact local energy and action continuity.",
      s.expand(energy_res), s.expand(action_res))

summary = dict(checks=len(checks),
               passed=sum(item["passed"] for item in checks),
               failed=sum(not item["passed"] for item in checks))
result = dict(
    construction="exterior spin comparison and SC-COV local completion",
    sympy_version=s.__version__, summary=summary,
    assumptions=[
        "Exterior r>L_g>0; static positive clock and positive spatial ruler metric.",
        "T1 chooses the torsion-free metric-compatible spatial spin lift.",
        "The finite holonomy comparison lies in one equatorial chart and is not a mechanical transport protocol.",
        "The local carrier process uses a selected constant-coefficient laboratory; no exterior trajectory is integrated.",
        "Wave continuity check is a nontrivial one-dimensional specialization; the full stated conservation proof uses integration by parts and no boundary flux."
    ],
    checks=checks)
out = Path(__file__).with_name("gravity_transport_results.json")
out.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2)+"\n")
print(json.dumps(summary), flush=True)
raise SystemExit(0 if not summary["failed"] else 1)
